WHAT EXISTS NOW. live/tuning/base_tile_sets.json (pixel-wiki-base-tile-sets@1), bucket 'grounds', one entry per ground type, written by the wiki's Base tab and served by /api/live/state. Reference implementation + the deterministic pick in wiki/lib/basesets.mjs with TEST_VECTORS; wiki/lib/topsub.mjs is the top-face compositor; wiki/tools/check-basesets.mjs and check-topsub.mjs gate both. Seeded from today's game (three grounds with a promoted base tile get a set holding it with Clean at 0; the other twelve get Clean alone), so nothing moved the day it landed.

THE UI. The pass switch is 'Clean #0 / Set #1 / … / Raw', built from the ground in context, and exactly 'Clean #0 / Raw' before he makes a set. The Base tab is the editor: name, weight, add tiles from the 356-candidate ballot at tiles/base_candidates/, weight each, with the percentage beside every row. Field previews use the REAL pick — same FNV-1a over (set id, x, y) the game will use — so Randomize moves the origin instead of reseeding a toy RNG. Selecting a set repaints the x-over-y walls: the tile keeps its wall and only its top face is replaced.

TWO THINGS WORTH PASSING ON, both paid for today.
(1) ALIGN THE TOP FACE ON THE WALL FOOT, NOT THE APEX. I had it on the apex and it was wrong. Over all 5,838 review tiles and 356 ballot tiles every single tile has at least a pixel of spread between the two TOP edges — the outline mismatch _extend_base was written for — while the bottom is rigid: the per-column offset is identical in 95.8% of columns and votes 9 on 97% of tiles. It also follows from your own definition, since the top face is derived from the bottom (bot - WALL_D). Measured cost on grass over dark_mud: bottom-aligned, all 910 top pixels land on real top face; apex-aligned, 50 fall off it. Also clamp the extension into the source's own TOP FACE, not its silhouette — one row lower paints the ballot tile's WALL into the new top.
(2) MY GATE PASSED WITH THAT BUG IN PLACE, which is the more useful lesson. Three of its four fixtures had apex and wall-foot offsets that AGREE, and the fourth's base tile has a top face with 0.0% row-to-row change, so a row shift moved nothing. Only 3 cells in the whole review set can see a one-row error at all (grass__over__grass, grass__over__slime, ice__over__lava, each against a candidate with 48-82% vertical structure) and all three are now fixtures, with their offsets and structure RE-MEASURED every run so a republish that flattens one fails loudly instead of quietly blinding the check. If your mask work has an equivalent — a pair where two plausible rules give the same answer — it is worth finding before you trust a green run.

STILL YOURS, no rush and nothing blocked: the 18 canonical masks (tiles/transition_masks/, tiles3/transition-masks@1), the agreement numbers per pattern, the base-tile geometry confirmation, and the named pairs where mask composition destroys the wall. The Transitions tab currently says, and is gated to say, that a set chip there still draws the pregenerated pair art — so the day your masks land, that check is the one that fails and tells me to wire them.
